source_read: PDF PDFs/Ketamine/Vollenweider_1997a_SRKetaminePET.pdf, all 14 pages (printed pp. 25-38), read in full from an own pdftotext -layout extraction; printed pp. 26, 27, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33 and 34 (Tables 1 and 2, Figs. 1-5 and the Results and Discussion text) re-checked on pages rendered at 150 dpi, because the PDF's text layer substitutes characters (= prints as 5, plus-minus as 6, minus as 2), so every number used here was read off the rendered page.

claims.overstatement: None for the part this source carries. The claim uses this paper only as a limit on how far the state resembles a psychiatric illness, and states it as the paper does: a comparison with published values, not with patients studied here.
claims.note: This source supports one sentence of the claim: that ego-pathology scores were about two thirds of published values for people with first-episode schizophrenia, that two of the five dimensions were clearly less affected, and that no patients were studied in this paper. All three parts check out on p. 34. The paper also independently supports the claim's general picture (a psychosis-like state during the infusion that was transient, p. 34) and its blinding qualifier (every participant recognised the (R)-ketamine condition as a drug effect, p. 36). Nothing in this source bears on the Beck, Krystal, Malhotra or Newcomer numbers.

anchors.extracted: Comparing mean Ego Pathology Inventory scores in this study with published scores in people with first-episode schizophrenia (Scharfetter, 1995): ego-consistency, ego-identity and ego-demarcation under (S)-ketamine were about two thirds of the patients' values, and ego-activity and ego-vitality were clearly less affected. No people with schizophrenia were studied in this paper; the comparison is with published figures. The authors conclude that ketamine can produce positive and negative symptoms in healthy volunteers but that there are also differences, particularly in the quality and quantity of ego-disorders, at the amounts tested.

The difficulty in reality appraisal and the impairment of ego-functioning under (S)-ketamine are described as transient and as varying in intensity between participants; participants, unlike people with schizophrenia, could at least in part recognise the derealisation and depersonalisation as abnormal and attribute them to the drug.

During the infusion: depersonalisation and derealisation, visual disturbances from pseudohallucinations to elementary and complex hallucinations, thought disorder and apathy on the APZ, AMDP and EPI; auditory changes were illusions (hyperacusis) rather than true hallucinations; directed attention and thinking became difficult; most participants showed flattened affect and became progressively emotionally withdrawn. n = 10 healthy volunteers, each their own control.

anchors.locator: Discussion › 4.3 Hyperfrontality and psychopathology, last paragraph
anchors.extracted: The (R)-ketamine state of relaxation and elation was correctly identified as a drug effect by all of the participants, although (R)-ketamine changed mood scores only with marginal significance. No blinding check of any kind is reported for either condition.

claims.overstatement: Two points. (a) The claim's opening generalisation, that brain activity 'goes up rather than down' while ketamine is being infused, is contradicted within this very source by its (R)-ketamine condition, where absolute glucose metabolism fell significantly in the temporomedial cortex bilaterally (-13.4%) and the left insula (-14%) and tended to fall whole-brain (-9.8%, P<0.07). The claim's own enantiomer claim carries that finding, but the imaging sentence as worded does not admit it, and 'ketamine' there means racemic and (S)-ketamine only. (b) 'both 1997 studies ... call the analysis exploratory' is exact for this paper (p. 29) but not for the companion, which says the correlational results are 'only preliminary' because of the small sample (1997b, p. 21); the substance is the same, the word is not.
claims.note: Every number the claim takes from this source checks out on p. 31: frontomedial 19.6%, frontolateral 20.1%, cingulate anterior 23.5%, cingulate posterior 24.0%, parietal 27.35% (each the mean of the left and right hemisphere), thalamus 17% at P<0.07, whole brain 12% at P<0.09 (not significant); cortical regions about 2-3 times more stimulated than subcortical ones (p. 29). The qualifier about correlation coefficients is correct and important: the Table 2 column headed r(sp) holds significance levels with a direction sign, not Spearman coefficients (the text's P<0.02 and P<0.001 for the frontolateral-putamen correlations with hallucinatory-disintegration appear in the table as -0.02 and -0.001), so no correlation coefficient is printed anywhere. The editors' estimate of 'about 150 to 180 comparisons' is not stated in either paper; my own tally of what is displayed or reported here alone (18 regions per hemisphere in absolute and relative form for two enantiomer conditions, 32 ratio tests in Table 2, the psychopathology scales and about 45 correlations) exceeds 180, so the estimate is conservative rather than inflated. One wording check: 'with no decrease in any region examined' (said of the companion paper) is true of absolute metabolism only; in both papers relative, whole-brain-normalised metabolism fell significantly in some posterior regions.

anchors.locator: Results › 3.3 Absolute and relative cerebral metabolic rates of glucose, 1st paragraph (continued from p. 29)
anchors.extracted: (S)-ketamine, n = 10, absolute CMRglu change from the person's own placebo scan, each figure the mean of the left and right hemisphere: frontomedial +19.6%, frontolateral +20.1%, cingulate anterior +23.5%, cingulate posterior +24.0%, parietal +27.35%. Somatosensory +21.1% and motor +23.0% significant in the left hemisphere only. Thalamus the only subcortical region with a bilateral increase, +17% at P<0.07. Whole brain +12%, P<0.09, not significant. Relative CMRglu rose bilaterally in frontomedial (7.7%), frontolateral (8.4%) and cingulate posterior (12.5%) cortex and in left parietal cortex (18.2%) and fell in left temporomedial cortex (4.8%), all P<0.05.

anchors.locator: Results › 3.3 Absolute and relative cerebral metabolic rates of glucose, 1st paragraph
anchors.extracted: The metabolic stimulation was not uniform: cortical regions were about 2-3 times more stimulated than subcortical regions, and within the cortex frontal regions about twice as much as posterior regions.

Wilcoxon matched-pairs tests and Spearman correlations; one a priori hypothesis (that (S)-ketamine would raise frontal CMRglu). No correction was made for the number of comparisons, and the authors state the results should be regarded as exploratory rather than confirmatory.

anchors.locator: Table 2 (correlations between changes of metabolic gradients and psychopathology scores, n = 10), column headed r(sp), with its footnote
anchors.extracted: The column headed r(sp) and described in the footnote as Spearman's rho holds values of -0.001 to -0.08 and +0.04 to +0.06, which are the significance levels given in the text with the sign of the direction: the frontolateral-putamen correlation with hallucinatory-disintegration appears in the text as P<0.02 (left) and P<0.001 (right) and in the table as -0.02 and -0.001. No correlation coefficient is printed anywhere in the paper, so the size of every symptom-to-metabolism association is unrecoverable. The footnote also states the values are not corrected for multiplicity.

anchors.locator: Results › 3.3 Absolute and relative cerebral metabolic rates of glucose, 2nd paragraph; Fig. 5 caption (p. 33)
anchors.extracted: In the same 10 people, equimolar (R)-ketamine tended to lower absolute CMRglu across regions: whole brain -9.8% (P<0.07, not significant), with significant decreases bilaterally in the temporomedial cortex (-13.4%) and in the left insula (-14%); relative CMRglu fell in the right temporal cortex (-4.0%) and bilaterally in the cerebellum (-5.0% and -4.0%), all P<0.05. So within this source one ketamine condition lowered, not raised, brain glucose metabolism.

anchors.extracted: All participants correctly identified the (R)-ketamine condition as a drug effect; each had also had a preliminary (S)-ketamine session before the PET phase (p. 28). No blinding check is reported.

claims.overstatement: One number and one inference. (a) The altered-states figure '37.0, SD 12.6' is the summary row printed in Table 1, but it does not match the ten per-person values printed above it, which give 38.2 (SD 10.3); the printed pair is exactly the racemic-study figure from the companion paper's Table 1 (37.00, SD 12.63), a different set of ten people. The claim repeats the paper's printed value without saying it is internally inconsistent. The ego-pathology pair (24.6, SD 11.8 against 1.3, SD 1.6) recomputes exactly, as does every editors' calculation. (b) 'the paper's description of the (S) condition as 60% of the racemic amount used earlier does not match the infusion rates printed in the two papers' is true of the rates but overstated as a conclusion: the per-minute maintenance rates are 67-70% of the companion study's and the induction step is 75% (15 mg against 20 mg), yet the (S) maintenance phase was 53 min against 60 min, so the total amount over a session works out at roughly 61-64% for a person of 70 kg, close to the stated 60%. The sound half of the claim's objection is the other half: no racemic condition was given to these same ten people, so the comparison with 'the racemic amount used earlier' is a comparison across two different samples.
claims.note: Everything else checks out. Design (p. 26, 2.2 and 2.6): within-person, described as placebo-controlled and counterbalanced, three PET scans a month apart, participants said to be blind to the conditions, (R) equimolar to (S). Symptoms, emotional reactions and mood scales (p. 29): euphoria or heightened feelings 30%, indifference 30%, heightened anxiety 40%; EWL deactivation P<0.01, introversion P<0.05, emotional irritability P<0.05, anxiety P<0.01; (R) produced no psychotic symptoms but relaxation, with OSE P<0.06, well-being P<0.09 and emotional irritation P<0.08. Blood levels (p. 29): (S) 269-523 ng/ml, mean 379 (SD 71); (R) 280-508, mean 389 (SD 74). Brain scans (p. 31, Fig. 5): (R) temporomedial -13.4% bilaterally and left insula -14%, whole brain -9.8% at P<0.07. Blinding (pp. 28, 34, 36): all ten recognised the (R) condition as a drug effect and all had had a preliminary (S)-ketamine session. Recomputations from Table 1 (p. 27): every one of the ten scored higher under (S) than under (R) on both global scales; within-person difference 22.6 points (SD 6.3) on the APZ global and 23.3 points (SD 10.9) on the EPI global; exact two-sided sign test with 10 of 10 positive gives P = 0.001953, that is 0.002. All three of the claim's editors' calculations reproduce exactly. Nothing in this source bears on the Yanagihara or Peltoniemi sentences.

anchors.locator: Materials and method › 2.2 Experimental design, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; and › 2.6 Phase II: PET studies (p. 28)
anchors.extracted: Within-person, described by the authors as placebo controlled and counterbalanced: ten healthy volunteers (6 men, 4 women, mean age 30.4, range 24-42), each receiving at monthly intervals three FDG-PET scans, a baseline (placebo), an (S)-ketamine and an (R)-ketamine scan, with participants stated to be blind to the conditions. Study conditions as printed: 15 mg of the enantiomer in 20 ml saline intravenously over 5 min, then 5 min with no further supply, then a continuous infusion at 0.014-0.02 mg/kg/min for 53 min; the (R) condition equimolar to the (S) condition; the (S) condition described as 60% of the racemic amount of the authors' earlier study, from an undescribed pilot potency ratio of about 1:0.6 mg/kg.

anchors.locator: Table 1, columns S-Ketamine and R-Ketamine (APZ global, EPI global), ten per-person rows
anchors.extracted: Per-person global scores. APZ global under (S): 25, 47, 27, 37, 46, 27, 38, 33, 47, 55; under (R): 10, 16, 9, 11, 15, 10, 8, 15, 29, 33. EPI global under (S): 10, 25, 25, 39, 24, 17, 27, 10, 21, 48; under (R): 0, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 1, 3, 5. Every one of the ten scored higher under (S) on both scales. My recomputation of the within-person differences: APZ 22.6 points (SD 6.3), EPI 23.3 points (SD 10.9); exact two-sided sign test, 10 of 10 positive, P = 0.002. The printed summary row for the (S) APZ column (mean 37.0, SD 12.6) does not follow from these ten values, which give 38.2 and 10.3; the printed EPI pair (24.6, 11.8) and both (R) pairs (15.6, 8.6 and 1.3, 1.6) do follow exactly.

(S): acute psychotic reactions with depersonalisation and derealisation, visual disturbances from pseudohallucinations to elementary and complex hallucinations, thought disorder and apathy; all participants reported distortion of body image, loosening of ego boundaries and altered sense of time and space, with heightened feelings or euphoria in 30%, indifference in 30% and heightened anxiety in 40%; EWL mood scores up for deactivation (P<0.01), introversion (P<0.05), emotional irritability (P<0.05) and anxiety (P<0.01). (R), same people: no psychotic symptoms, a state of relaxation, with a small non-significant rise in oceanic boundlessness (P<0.06), well-being (P<0.09) and a slight fall in emotional irritation (P<0.08).

Plasma concentrations during the scans: (S) 269-523 ng/ml, mean 379 (SD 71); (R) 280-508 ng/ml, mean 389 (SD 74); levels stayed within the same range of magnitude during the infusion. Psychotic symptoms appeared about 5 min after the start of the (S) infusion at a mean plasma level of 539 ng/ml, which is above the top of the stated (S) range on the same page.

anchors.locator: Results › 3.3 Absolute and relative cerebral metabolic rates of glucose, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Figs. 4 (p. 32) and 5 (p. 33)
anchors.extracted: Opposite directions in the same people: (S) raised absolute CMRglu in most regions (frontomedial +19.6% to parietal +27.35%), while (R) tended to lower it, whole brain -9.8% (P<0.07, not significant), with significant decreases bilaterally in the temporomedial cortex (-13.4%) and the left insula (-14%).

(R)-ketamine did not produce psychotic symptoms but relaxation and a feeling of well-being; participants could well tell the (R) condition from the placebo condition; the rise in oceanic boundlessness was apparent in five of the ten. The authors infer from the (S) condition being 60% of a racemic amount and producing virtually the same psychotic reactions as racemic ketamine that (S)-ketamine is the predominant psychotomimetically active agent in racemic ketamine; the racemic comparison is with the companion study's different sample, not with a racemic condition in these ten people.

anchors.locator: Materials and method › 2.2 Experimental design (p. 26) and › 2.5 Phase I: Preliminary drug exposure (p. 28), compared with Vollenweider et al. 1997b › 2.2 (p. 11)
anchors.extracted: Editors'-calculation check of the '60% of the racemic amount' statement against the printed conditions. Here: 15 mg induction, then 0.014-0.02 mg/kg/min for 53 min. Companion paper: 20 mg induction, then 0.02-0.03 mg/kg/min for 60 min. Ratios: induction 75%, maintenance rate 67-70%, but total over a session (induction plus maintenance, 53 min against 60 min) about 61-64% at a body weight of 70 kg. Separately, every participant had already had a psychotomimetic (S)-ketamine session in phase I before the PET phase began.

key_findings.correction: Recomputed independently from the ten per-person pairs: 22.6 (SD 6.3) and 23.3 (SD 10.9), all ten higher under (S), exact two-sided sign test P = 0.002 (2/1024 = 0.001953). The note that the printed (S) APZ mean and SD (37.0, 12.6) do not follow from the column, which gives 38.2 and 10.3, is also confirmed. The card's 95% confidence intervals and standardised paired differences were not recomputed here.
Checked row by row against Table 2 on the rendered page: (S) fronto-temporal 6.8-14.0%, fronto-occipital 9.1-11.7%, left FL-CA 16.0%, right FM-PU 12.3%, right FL-PU 13.2%; (R) 0.1-7.4%. All correct.

reporting_issues.note: Found independently before the card was opened, by the same route: the ten values give 38.2 (SD 10.3) against the printed 37.0 (SD 12.6), and the printed pair is the companion paper's racemic figure (37.00, 12.63, p. 11 of 1997b). The other three summary pairs in the same table reproduce exactly.
Also found independently. Verified on the rendered p. 33: the text's P<0.02 and P<0.001 for the frontolateral-putamen correlations are the table's -0.02 and -0.001.
Both figures read off the rendered p. 29: range 269-523 ng/ml, onset value 539 ng/ml.

The arithmetic is right but the consequence is too strong. Induction 15 mg against 20 mg is 75% and the maintenance rate 0.014-0.02 against 0.02-0.03 mg/kg/min is 67-70%, as the card says; but the (S) maintenance phase ran 53 min against the companion study's 60 min, so the total amount over a session comes to about 61-64% at 70 kg, which is consistent with the stated 60%. The ratio therefore does match the printed conditions once the shorter infusion is counted. What does undercut the inference is that no racemic condition was given to these ten people, so the comparison is across two samples; the card's own interpretation_gap section says this, and the reporting issue should rest on it rather than on the arithmetic.
Verified on the rendered p. 27: the third APZ subscale is printed as OSE ('visionary restructuralization') where VUS is meant.

Verified against Table 2 on the rendered p. 33: of the four fronto-occipital entries only left FL-OL carries a (P<0.05); left FM-OM is tr and both right-hemisphere entries are ns, while the text claims a significant increase of about 10% in both hemispheres.
Abstract p. 25 '3-4 time higher affinity'; Introduction p. 26 '4 to 5 times higher affinity'; both cite Oye et al. (1991).
Ages 30, 40, 30, 42, 26, 24, 25, 34, 24, 28 sum to 303, mean 30.3 against the printed 30.4.
Figs. 1 and 2 on the rendered p. 30: the in-figure titles say mean plus-minus SD and both captions say mean plus-minus S.D. and then that the boxes indicate mean plus-minus S.E.
Verified on the rendered p. 33: the (R)-ketamine left FM-TL cell carries a capital A, undefined in the footnote.

risk_of_bias.note: RoB 2 is the right instrument for a placebo-controlled within-person laboratory study with counterbalanced order (METHODS 5.3), the domain judgments match what the paper reports, and the overall judgment of high is no less severe than the worst domain. I would reach the same two high domains for the same reasons: a blind the authors themselves report as broken (p. 36), and selective reporting of a large uncorrected set with no protocol. One addition to the deviations domain: the failure of the blind is worse than a single unblinded condition, because every participant had already experienced (S)-ketamine in phase I, so the placebo scan was the only condition none of them had a template for.

interpretation_gap.note: Substantial is right, and the card names the two steps correctly. I would add one: the abstract reports the symptom-to-metabolism correlations as findings without saying that no correlation coefficient appears anywhere in the paper, so a reader cannot tell whether a correlation marked P<0.05 in ten people is large or small.

missed: Fig. 2's caption (p. 30) says (S)-ketamine significantly increased scores for 'emotional irritability' and 'anxiety', while the Results text on p. 29 reports four significant EWL scales: deactivation (P<0.01), introversion (P<0.05), emotional irritability (P<0.05) and anxiety (P<0.01). The caption and the text do not agree about how many mood scales changed, and the figure is the only place the scale-by-scale data appear.

The pilot study that fixed the (S) amount at 60% of the racemic amount, and with it the whole equipotency premise, is given in one sentence (p. 26) with no sample size, no method and no reference; it appears to be unpublished. The card records the 1:0.6 ratio but not that its source is undescribed.

The (R)-ketamine condition is reported as equimolar to the (S) condition, but no molar calculation, salt form or measured concentration check is given for either preparation beyond 1 mg/ml in 0.9% NaCl (p. 27); the measured plasma concentrations (379 against 389 ng/ml) are the only evidence that the two conditions were in fact comparable, and the card could cite them in that role.
